subject: Polity
description: Articles 14-32, six fundamental rights, landmark judgments

questions.stem: Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution are enshrined in:
questions.explanation: Part III — Fundamental Rights (Arts 12-35). Part II — Citizenship (5-11). Part IV — DPSP (36-51). Part IV-A — Fundamental Duties (51A). Inspired by the US Bill of Rights.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Currently, how many CATEGORIES of Fundamental Rights are there in the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Six Fundamental Rights: (1) Right to Equality (14-18), (2) Right to Freedom (19-22), (3) Right against Exploitation (23-24), (4) Right to Freedom of Religion (25-28), (5) Cultural and Educational Rights (29-30), (6) Right to Constitutional Remedies (32). The Right to Property was demoted from FR to legal right under Article 300A by the 44th Amendment, 1978.
questions.subject: Polity

options.option_text: Equality before the law and equal protection of the laws

questions.explanation: Article 14 — 'The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.' Applies to all persons (not just citizens). Article 15 — prohibition of discrimination; Article 17 — abolition of untouchability; Article 19 — six freedoms; Article 21 — right to life and personal liberty.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) was expanded by the SC in MANEKA GANDHI v. UNION OF INDIA (1978) to include:

options.option_text: The right to live with dignity — including many 'implicit' rights (clean environment, livelihood, education etc.)

questions.explanation: Maneka Gandhi (1978) — the SC held that 'procedure established by law' under Article 21 must also be fair, just, reasonable. Subsequent cases have unfolded 'the right to life' into right to privacy (Puttaswamy 2017), education (UC Hyderabad), dignity, clean environment, speedy trial, livelihood, shelter etc.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Match the ARTICLE with its SUBJECT. A. Article 17.  B. Article 19.  C. Article 23.  D. Article 25. List-II: 1. Abolition of untouchability.  2. Six freedoms (speech, assembly, etc.).  3. Prohibition of human trafficking and forced labour.  4. Freedom of religion.
questions.explanation: Art 17 — untouchability abolished, its practice forbidden. Art 19(1) — six freedoms: speech & expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession. Art 23 — prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour. Art 25 — freedom of conscience and free profession/propagation of religion.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which FR is available only to INDIAN CITIZENS (not to aliens)?
questions.explanation: Arts 15, 16, 19, 29, 30 — only citizens. Art 14 (equality), 20 (protection against ex-post-facto laws etc.), 21 (life & liberty), 22 (protection from arrest/detention), 25-28 (religion) — available to 'ANY PERSON', including foreigners.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Fundamental Right did Dr. Ambedkar call 'the heart and soul of the Constitution'?
questions.explanation: Art 32 — the right to move the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Ambedkar: 'If I was asked to name any particular article in this Constitution as the most important — an article without which this Constitution would be a nullity — I could not refer to any other article except this one. It is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.'
